html:
A South Korean business group founded in 1938 by Lee Byung-chul as a small trading company in Daegu. It grew into the largest of Korea's family-run conglomerates, the chaebol, and the world's biggest maker of memory chips.

Lee's firm first sold dried fish, vegetables and noodles. After the Korean War it went into sugar refining, wool, insurance and retail, with help from the government's push for industry. In 1969 it began making electronics, at first cheap televisions and fridges.

In 1974 Samsung bought into chip making, and from the 1980s it poured money into memory chips. By the early 1990s it led the world in them. Lee's son Lee Kun-hee, chairman from 1987, pushed hard on quality. Its Galaxy phones made it one of the largest phone makers.

Samsung is a large share of South Korea's exports and economy. With TSMC in Taiwan it makes many of the world's most advanced chips, part of the rise of South Korea as an industrial power.
